name: Smok
isnote: English Wikipedia places Smok in Paracrocodylomorpha without a family; the backbone kept it in Poposauroidea, unresolved within it.
sum: Smok is a large predatory pseudosuchian from the latest Triassic of Lisowice, southern Poland, first described as a theropod dinosaur.
wsnote: About 5-6 m long with a skull 50-60 cm long (English Wikipedia); estimates, not measurements.
holotype: ZPAL V.33/15, a partially complete braincase associated with a partially preserved skeleton, from Lisowice, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland.
material: The holotype and further material from Lisowice; a second occurrence in southern Poland is reported by Niedźwiedzki and Budziszewska-Karwowska (2018).
biology: A large predator; a 2019 study (Qvarnström and colleagues) reports tyrannosaurid-like bone eating in a Triassic archosaur, according to its title. Fuller details are not read here.
author: Niedźwiedzki et al. 2012

sources.text: Niedźwiedzki, G., Sulej, T. and Dzik, J. 2012. A large predatory archosaur from the Late Triassic of Poland. Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 57(2): 251–256.
Niedźwiedzki, G. and Budziszewska-Karwowska, E. 2018. A new occurrence of the Late Triassic archosaur Smok in southern Poland. Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 63(4): 703–712.
Qvarnström, M., Ahlberg, P. E. and Niedźwiedzki, G. 2019. Tyrannosaurid-like osteophagy by a Triassic archosaur. Scientific Reports 9(1): 925.
Dzik, J., Sulej, T. and Niedźwiedzki, G. 2008. A dicynodont-theropod association in the latest Triassic of Poland. Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 53(4): 733–738.

dates_note: No PBDB occurrences. Age 208.5-205 Ma (latest Norian to early Rhaetian) from the English Wikipedia summary of the Lisowice site.
